beats.text: A customer asks your A.I. assistant about refunds.
It answers, confidently: ninety days. Your policy says thirty.
Would you even know it happened?
Fix found: Lang fuse.
Think of it as a flight recorder for your A.I. app.
It's open source, with more than thirty-six thousand stars on GitHub.
You add a few lines of code to your app.
From then on, every question, every answer, and every step in between is saved as a trace.
Later, you can open any conversation and see exactly what happened.
One. Trace a complaint. Find the exact conversation, the prompt that was sent, and what the model said back.
Two. Watch your spend. It tracks tokens and cost for every call, with prices built in for popular models.
Three. Score the answers. Collect thumbs up and thumbs down from users, or let another model grade them, so the bad answers rise to the top.
Now, the catch.
The core is M.I.T. licensed, but a few enterprise features sit in their own folder and need a license key.
And self-hosting means running several services: a web app, a worker, two databases, a cache, and file storage. Or you pay for their cloud, which has a free tier.
It's worth it once real customers talk to your A.I.
For a weekend prototype, it's probably more than you need.
Want an alternative? Take a look at Arize Phoenix.
To try it, clone the repo and run docker compose up. It's running on your own machine in about five minutes.
What problem should we fix next? Tell us in the comments.
